subsystems.name: Targeting module
subsystems.role: finds the exact DNA address and nicks just one strand.

subsystems.name: Writing module
subsystems.role: copies a new sequence from an RNA template into the DNA.
parts: linker peptide joining the two proteins

subsystems.name: pegRNA
subsystems.role: the guide that both addresses the site and carries the replacement text.

subsystems.name: Nick guidance and repair tuning
subsystems.role: a second cut or a repair-suppressing protein biases the cell toward keeping the edit.

subsystems.name: Delivery vehicle
subsystems.role: gets the editor into the right cells and no others.
parts: electroporation for cells removed from the body

subsystems.name: Cell repair machinery
subsystems.role: the host's own flap and ligation enzymes actually finish the edit.

buildSteps.title: Choose the edit
buildSteps.detail: Decide the exact bases to change — a point mutation, a small insertion or a small deletion — and check what else in the genome looks similar.

buildSteps.title: Design the pegRNA
buildSteps.detail: A software model picks the spacer, the primer binding site that will grip the nicked strand, and the template that spells out the new sequence.

buildSteps.title: Make the editor
buildSteps.detail: The nickase and reverse transcriptase genes are fused into one construct, produced as protein or as mRNA in a manufacturing facility.

buildSteps.title: Package and deliver
buildSteps.detail: For cells taken from a patient the payload goes in by electroporation; for treatment inside the body it is wrapped in lipid nanoparticles or a viral capsid that targets a chosen tissue.

buildSteps.title: Nick and prime
buildSteps.detail: Inside the nucleus the complex binds its target and cuts only the strand carrying the PAM; the freed 3' end pairs with the pegRNA's primer binding site.

buildSteps.title: Write the new sequence
buildSteps.detail: The reverse transcriptase extends that 3' end using the pegRNA template, building a flap of DNA that contains the desired edit.

buildSteps.title: Resolve the flap
buildSteps.detail: The cell's own enzymes equilibrate the new and old flaps, remove the unedited one and ligate the edited strand into place.

buildSteps.title: Bias the outcome
buildSteps.detail: A second nick on the opposite strand, or temporary suppression of mismatch repair, makes the cell keep the edited version rather than reverting it.

buildSteps.title: Verify
buildSteps.detail: Targeted and whole-genome sequencing confirms the intended edit and checks for unintended changes before any clinical use.

prerequisites.why: prime editing reuses the same address-finding machinery, adapted so it nicks rather than cuts both strands.
the writing step is an RNA-to-DNA copy, an enzyme class borrowed from retroviruses and engineered for accuracy.
a pegRNA is a longer, more structured guide than standard CRISPR guide RNA and must be made to high purity.
editing the right cells inside the body, especially outside the liver, is the main obstacle to treating most diseases.
the cell decides whether to keep the edit, so efficiency depends on understanding flap and mismatch repair.

prerequisites.tech: Long-term safety data on genome editors
prerequisites.why: off-target edits and large rearrangements must be ruled out over years, not months.

pathway.milestone: prime editing used widely as a research tool in cells, organoids and animals; base editing and first-generation CRISPR therapies already reaching patients
pathway.unlocks: proof that precise, break-free editing works, and a regulatory path for edited cell therapies.

pathway.milestone: first human trials of prime-edited cells for blood and immune disorders
pathway.unlocks: real safety and durability data in people, using ex vivo editing where delivery is easiest.

pathway.milestone: in vivo prime editing of liver and other organs, and larger edits via twin prime editing or integrase-assisted insertion
pathway.unlocks: one-off treatments for metabolic and genetic liver disease.

pathway.milestone: multi-edit and organ-targeted treatments at scale
pathway.unlocks: correcting several mutations at once, and reaching tissues such as muscle, lung or nerve where delivery is still unsolved.
